newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco dips in red on trade, tourism rises.
newsitem.headline: Morocco dips in red on trade, tourism rises.

text.p: Morocco moved deeper into the red with its trade deficit in the first half of 1996 over the same period last year, after being hit by severe drought and needing to import food for its 27 million people.

The gap between imports and exports in the period rose to 13.87 billion dirhams ($1.59 billion), an increase of 4.1 percent, according to the official Office des Changes, the country's regulatory trade body.
But tourists visiting the North African country in the first half of this year spent 5.15 billion dirhams ($592 million), up 25.7 percent on the same time last year.
Moroccans living abroad remitted 8.24 billion dirhams between January and June this year, a rise of 2.7 percent or 220 million dirhams from 8.02 billion.

The bulk of remittances came from Moroccans based in France with 63 percent of the total, followed by those in the Benelux countries, 8.4 percent, Italy, Germany and the Netherlands. Remittances from the Arab World were headed by those from the United Arab Emirates, 2.9 percent, and Saudi Arabia 2.0 percent.

In a detailed breakdown of first half 1996 imports and exports, the Office des Changes said in its latest bulletin that imports totalled 41.72 billion dirhams ($4.79 billion) against 40.84 billion for the first six months of 1995.
Exports for the two periods were respectively 27.85 billion dirhams and 27.51 billion.

Food imports jumped 24.5 percent in value to total 5.91 billion dirhams ($680 million) mainly through wheat and maize purchases. In volume, the rise was limited to 2.3 percent -- 2.01 million tonnes against 1.97 million.
Wheat imports more than doubled in cost to 2.33 billion dirhams ($268 million) from 1.21 billion dirhams, while maize imports were 482.7 million dirhams from 337.3 million.

Morocco was hit by severe drought during its 1994/95 cereal season and analysts estimated cereal output then at around 1.7 million tonnes. The agriculture ministry last August estimated it would import around 1.0 million tonnes of soft wheat for the 1996/97 season.
The cost of imported consumer goods rose to 4.64 billion dirhams against 3.89 billion, an increase of 19.3 percent.
